# Standards-Alignment Terminology Disposition

## Status and boundary

This is a non-normative audit artefact. It does not amend a Caelestis instrument, revive retired terms, create a canonical family, or determine the meaning of historical records.

The current audit baseline includes the merged AEON-003 refactor (PR #104). The FM-0048 branch (PR #105) is inspected as an active stacked baseline only; its Draft status does not make it adopted corpus fact.

---

## 1. Retired composed-architecture family

`AEON.CC`, `Instrumenta`, `Collectiva`, and `Cognitiva` are correctly treated as retired from current classification. The deterministic residual scan finds no current normative occurrence of the exact former class family or class names.

The residual scan intentionally does not treat terms such as *instrumentalisation* as a retired-class match.

No semantic reconstruction or automatic migration is authorised. Historical references remain governed by the corpus version in force when they were created.

---

## 2. `Primaria` and `Derivata`

The current normative corpus has no exact residual occurrence. They remain retired origin-class labels and must not be reintroduced through examples, schemas, validator allow-lists or display fields.

---

## 3. Singular-arbitration residual

The residual scan records one phrase-match for singular-arbitration terminology. It is a non-collapse statement in Annex B: arbitration remains a constitutional function and does not require a singular, unified or model-internal engine.

This is not a reintroduction of the retired assumption. Future review should preserve that distinction and avoid treating a local component labelled an “arbitration engine” as a universal architectural prerequisite.

---

## 4. Dyadic, triadic and polyadic language

The generated residual scan records 231 current textual matches across the normative corpus baseline. The words often carry intelligible content—number of participating parties, authority concentration, propagation, coordination, and third-party effect—but they are not established controlled terminology in the reviewed ISO, NIST, SPDX, CycloneDX, Singapore or EU sources.

### Determination

The causal mechanisms are retained for review; the cardinality vocabulary is not recommended for retention as current metadata, canonical classification or a source-authoritative doctrine name.

### Proposed replacement vocabulary

| Current wording | Current-use replacement | Meaning to preserve |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dyadic | two-party configuration | one-to-one interaction or authority relationship |
| triadic | three-party configuration | interaction or authority relationship involving three relevant parties |
| polyadic | multi-party / multi-actor configuration | a relationship or governance condition involving more than three relevant parties, systems or institutions |
| polyadic amplification | multi-party amplification | propagation or reinforcement across participants, systems or organisational contexts |
| polyadic authority | multi-party / cross-institutional authority | authority extending beyond a bounded two-party relationship |

### Migration constraint

This is not a mechanical find-and-replace task. Some occurrences are historical ledger text, quoted titles, defined symbolic labels, or narrowly relational prose. A repair pass must classify each occurrence before mutation, retain version-bound historical wording where required, regenerate all indexes, and confirm that no causal safeguard is weakened.

---

## 5. Entity and identity terms

`identity`, `continuity`, `formation`, `agent`, `system`, `model`, `instance`, `substrate`, and `registry` are all active terms, but their co-occurrence does not supply a controlled entity threshold. The taxonomy work must therefore be separated from claims about consciousness, sentience, legal personhood, sovereignty, or moral status.

The existing distinction is sound:

* a registry is not personhood;
* a substrate identifier is not identity continuity;
* architecture is not proof of subjective phenomenology; and
* a classification threshold must be independently evidenced.
